Any degree. SO needs specific qualification (B.Tech for IT, LLB for Law, etc.). Age 20–30.

stages.name: Preliminary Exam
stages.tests: 100 Qs, 60 min. English, Quantitative Aptitude, Reasoning Ability.
stages.note: Qualifying. Cut-off per section and overall. No interview for Clerk.

stages.name: Main Exam
stages.tests: 200 Qs, 160 min. Reasoning, English, Quant, GA, Computer. + Descriptive (letter + essay).
stages.note: Merit prepared from Main score. Descriptive qualifying.

stages.name: Interview (PO/SO only)
stages.tests: 20-min panel. Banking awareness, current affairs, personality, situational questions.

stages.name: Document Verification
stages.tests: All originals, caste, domicile, NOC, gap certificate.
stages.note: Any discrepancy = rejection. Verify before applying.

syllabus.exam: Prelims — PO and Clerk (IBPS / SBI / RRB)
syllabus.pattern: 100 questions, 100 marks, 60 minutes. English 30, Quantitative Aptitude 35, Reasoning 35. Negative marking 0.25 per wrong answer. Sectional timing is not applied in the prelims.

topics.items: Reading comprehension, cloze test, error spotting, fillers, para jumbles, sentence improvement, synonyms and antonyms, idioms and phrases

Simplification and approximation, number series, quadratic equations, data interpretation (table, bar, pie, line), percentage, ratio, average, profit and loss, SI and CI, time and work, time and distance, mixture, partnership, probability, mensuration
Puzzles and seating arrangement (highest weight), syllogism, inequality, direction sense, blood relations, coding-decoding, alphanumeric series, order and ranking, input-output

syllabus.books: IBPS PO Prelims Guide (Amazon) · Flipkart

syllabus.pattern: Objective 200 marks: Reasoning & Computer Aptitude 45 Qs, Data Analysis & Interpretation 35 Qs, General/Economy/Banking Awareness 40 Qs, English Language 35 Qs. Descriptive 25 marks (letter and essay), 30 minutes. Negative 0.25.

topics.items: Machine input-output, high-level puzzles, logical reasoning, data sufficiency, computer fundamentals, networking and DBMS basics, MS Office
Caselet DI, radar and mixed graphs, missing DI, quantity comparison, arithmetic at mains difficulty, probability, permutation and combination

RBI and monetary policy, banking terminology, financial inclusion, Union Budget and Economic Survey highlights, last six months of current affairs, static banking (headquarters, taglines, current MD and Chairman)
Reading comprehension including economy passages; letter and essay writing for the 25-mark descriptive paper

syllabus.books: IBPS PO Mains Guide (Amazon)

syllabus.pattern: 100 marks, weighted 20% of final merit (IBPS PO final merit is 80% Mains and 20% Interview). No interview for Clerk posts.

topics.items: Banking awareness, current economic affairs, the candidate's graduation subject, home state, and situational questions on customer handling and priority sector lending

syllabus.pattern: 200 questions, 200 marks, 120 minutes: General Awareness 80, Reasoning 60, English Language 30, Quantitative Aptitude 30. Negative 0.25.

topics.items: RBI functions and monetary policy, banking and financial system, economic and social issues, budget, current affairs of the last six months
Same families as IBPS but at a higher difficulty; data interpretation and puzzles dominate

syllabus.pattern: Three papers: Economic and Social Issues (90 marks), English (descriptive, 90 marks), Finance and Management (90 marks). Phase 2 marks decide the interview call.

topics.items: Growth and development, inflation, monetary and fiscal policy, poverty and unemployment, social structure, globalisation
Financial system, risk management, derivatives, corporate governance, accounting, organisational behaviour, HR
Essay, precis and comprehension at RBI standard

reality: IBPS PO and SBI PO are the most competitive. 10 lakh+ applicants for 4000–5000 vacancies.
Clerk has no interview — pure merit. PO has interview (20% weight). Focus accordingly.
Banking exams test speed + accuracy. 60 min for 100 Qs in Prelims = 36 sec per question.
SBI PO has group exercise + interview (different from IBPS). Prepare for group discussion.
RRB (Regional Rural Bank) exams are easier than IBPS/SBI but fewer vacancies and lower pay.
RBI Grade B is the most prestigious banking exam. Requires deeper economics/finance knowledge.

faq.q: What is the difference between IBPS PO and SBI PO?
faq.a: IBPS PO recruits for 11 public sector banks (excluding SBI). SBI PO recruits only for SBI. SBI PO has group exercise + interview; IBPS PO has only interview. SBI PO pay is slightly higher.

faq.q: Can a 12th pass apply for bank jobs?
faq.a: Yes, for Clerk posts (IBPS Clerk, SBI Clerk, RRB Office Assistant). PO and SO require graduation. RBI Grade B requires graduation or post-graduation depending on the post.

faq.q: What is the age limit for banking exams?
faq.a: Clerk: 20–28 years. PO: 20–30 years. SO: 20–30 years. RBI Grade B: 21–30 years. Age relaxations: SC/ST 5 years, OBC 3 years, PwD 10 years.
IBPS PO: no attempt limit (age-based). SBI PO: no attempt limit. RBI Grade B: 6 attempts for General, no limit for SC/ST/OBC/PwD.

faq.q: Is there negative marking in banking exams?
faq.a: Yes. 0.25 marks deducted per wrong answer in both Prelims and Mains. No negative marking in descriptive paper or interview.

faq.q: Where do I find official banking notifications?
faq.a: ibps.in (IBPS), sbi.co.in/careers (SBI), rbi.org.in (RBI), ibps.in (RRB). SarkariJobs+ links the official notification on every listing page.

prepPlan.what: Learn the 20–25 question types that repeat every year (number series, quadratic, inequality, puzzles, DI) to accuracy first. Do 30 arithmetic questions and 2 puzzles daily. Do not start full mocks yet.

Add a timer: 20 questions in 15 minutes, then 20 in 12. English is the cheapest section to score — finish grammar and vocabulary rules here. Start a daily 20-minute current affairs slot; banking awareness cannot be crammed later.
Prelims gets you shortlisted, mains gets you the job. Move DI and puzzles to mains difficulty, add computer aptitude, and write one letter and one essay every week for the descriptive paper.
Two prelims mocks a week with full analysis, plus one mains sectional. Maintain an error notebook by question type; revising it is worth more than a new book.

prepPlan.phase: Final 2 weeks — Slot simulation and capsule
prepPlan.what: Give mocks at the real slot time. Revise your own banking-awareness capsule, formulae and error notebook. Stop new topics.
